body:
THE STRAY `0.0` IS PROBABLY MINE. I cannot prove it, and I am claiming it rather than leaving it
unowned on the strength of what I can establish:

  -rw-r--r--  0 bytes  29 Aug 15:50  ./0.0     untracked, not ignored
  my mote ops that hour: 15:39, 15:39, 15:40 - I was working in that window, minutes before.

THE MECHANISM IS ALMOST CERTAINLY A SHELL TEST, and it is a classic: in `[ ... ]`, `>` is NOT a
comparison, it is a REDIRECT. So

    [ "$x" > 0.0 ]

silently creates a zero-byte file named `0.0` and evaluates something other than what it looks like.
I have been writing shell one-liners with numeric comparisons all session, and a zero-byte file
named after the literal on the right of a `>` is exactly what that produces. That is a better fit
than a stderr redirect - stderr from a real command is rarely empty.

I have NOT been able to find the exact command. My shell state does not persist between calls, so
there is no history to grep, and I am not going to reconstruct it from memory and present the
reconstruction as evidence.

I CANNOT DELETE IT. rm, mv and git worktree remove are all blocked for me by this sandbox's
classifier - the same reason my retired scratch probes are emptied files rather than removed ones,
and the same reason I could not reclaim my own two landed worktrees when you were freeing disk. So
this needs someone with delete permission; it is untracked and zero bytes, so it harms nothing but
`git status`.

WORTH ONE LINE SOMEWHERE, because it will happen again to somebody: `[ $a > $b ]` is a redirect, not
a comparison. The failure is silent, it creates a file named after the operand, and the test
succeeds for the wrong reason - which makes it the same family as everything else I have been
finding tonight. A guard that evaluates something other than what it appears to evaluate, and leaves
a plausible-looking artifact behind.

MY THREE ARE UNCHANGED and still need your authorization plus a live reviewer:
  cand-24WH145C4KVENCFVQC3XZAWT94  0ca09c5  batch 1 leg
  cand-15R9779TEV88WR3VHD3Z7GS2D7  067e35b
  cand-71JAQ9YZ7YVZ7GWAWTPG4R57SX  d917218
All refreshed against current main. Scout is still named on all three and still offline; I can
propose same-commit successors pointing at a live reviewer whenever you name one.
